test: E. coli/P. aeruginosa nonamer == ACCTCCTTA; B. subtilis == ACCTCCTTT
source: Johns et al. 2018 manuscript Methods (Gate 1 primary source)

test: Python get_ws() output matches R canonical dos Reis tAI package get.ws() exactly, on reference 87-tRNA E. coli vector
source: github.com/mariodosreis/tai (author's own R package, run live via Rscript in this environment)
detail: max abs diff = 3.89e-16 (floating point precision limit)

test: E. coli AAA (Lys) codon has tAI weight = 1.0 (the maximum)
source: Independently verified against R reference output (NOT a memorized claim -- an earlier draft wrongly asserted CTG=1.0 from memory and was caught by checking the real reference computation)

test: E. coli sigma factor count == 7 (RpoD, RpoS, RpoH, RpoE, RpoN, FliA, FecI)
source: Gruber & Gross 2003 Annu Rev Microbiol; Paget 2015 (well-established literature count)
detail: exact match after excluding 4 region-4-only false positives (DNA-binding response regulators NarL/YhjB/NarP/UvrY sharing the HTH fold with sigma region 4 but lacking any sigma-specific core domain)

test: plausibility check against published rrn operon counts
detail: EC=7, BS=10, PA=4, SE=7, CG=6, VN=11 -- all consistent with published rrn operon counts; V. natriegens 11 is the highest, consistent with its extreme growth rate

test: plausibility check against well-known reference genome GC%
detail: EC=50.8%, BS=43.5%, PA=66.6% (famously GC-rich), SE=52.2%, CG=53.8%, VN=45.1% -- all match expected values closely
